doc.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024

chapter: Studio work and learning the craft
title: Modern classical music and Henry Pleasants
summary: Discussion of how difficult modern classical music is, Pleasants' The Agony of Modern Music, composers needing to explain their music, and a mistranslated Royal Garden Blues.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Do you think modern classical music is — I’m not sure where “modern” starts but — more difficult to play than the classics, the Romantic period and Baroque music? That’s a wide question but I once had an experience playing a Honegger piece and there was a saxophone part and man I could not keep track of where it was. It was so harmonically dense and of course they had 60 bars of rest before I came in and talk about sweating. Please give me a cue.

Yeah. Well you know you’re getting into a controversial area you know. There was a book called — now I can’t remember, damn — The Agony of Modern Music by Henry Pleasants. And he said the real modern music is jazz, because like from Stravinsky on you know it got so complicated with different time signatures and it’s like a made-up idiom sort of because the complexity of playing contemporary music, it’s like you don’t know what style — I mean you have to learn the style of each individual composer but it’s like — you know — complicated. It’s a specific skill you have to — I don’t want to —

It seems like the music composition in the classical world keeps trying to do something new and I think it might have to do with getting a grant — getting grants to write new work and how far can you go and still do something new? And what we get is what maybe you’re struggling to find in your description.

Well I have my own opinion about some of that stuff but you know a lot of guys specialize in it and they’re happy doing that. I have an example, there was a series called “Music From Japan” and they used to display the scores in the lobby, you know, under glass. And Henry Pleasants, in this book he mentions like composers, they have to get a © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
teaching job so they can explain their music you know. They’ve got to explain the music, man.
You didn’t have to explain that Dixieland music, did you?

No. No, not to the Japanese people. The funny thing is the host of this thing the other night was saying — the leader asked her to translate what he was saying. And he said, “We’re going to play a tune from a place in Chicago called the Royal Garden, it’s the ‘Royal Garden Blues.’” And so she said, “They’re going to play ‘Royal Garden Brews.” So it’s like about beer, you know?
